T1.objective: Explore OpenMP work decomposition without changing the scalar pixel recurrence. Contrast static contiguous rows with dynamic/guided row scheduling and, if useful, a contiguous 2D tiled or collapsed-loop partition to test whether row granularity leaves imbalance within expensive rows. Vary chunk sizes only as measured experiments. Use a serial path when it avoids one-thread overhead; never exceed `threads` or change global OpenMP settings. Preserve the original float coordinate and recurrence behavior, write every output, and do not specialize to tested bounds or dimensions. Validate smaller and shifted-bound cases; measure native wall time at one and four cores, including scheduling overhead at n=1024.
T1.subject: Thread-budgeted OpenMP work decomposition

T2.objective: Develop an exact SIMD kernel across adjacent x pixels, with correct active-lane handling and tails. Preserve not only the recurrence but also the original float coordinate calculation (`dx`, `dy`, `x0 + i*dx`, `y0 + j*dy`); do not replace it with an incrementally accumulated or otherwise differently rounded grid. Do not change compiler flags or assume an ISA feature merely from the architecture label: verify the candidate builds and runs under the frozen configuration, and report unavailable variants. Validate exact iteration counts for smaller and shifted bounds as well as the target case. Keep scheduling changes out of this experiment so its one-thread SIMD contribution remains identifiable; report the four-core-budget result without implying it uses four cores.
T2.subject: Exact SIMD across independent pixels

T3.objective: Explore scalar interleaving of small groups of independent pixel states to expose instruction-level parallelism, without explicit SIMD intrinsics or OpenMP scheduling changes. Compare the sequential baseline with a few group widths (for example, 2, 4, and 8), including a non-divisible tail and pixels with differing escape lengths. Preserve each pixel’s escape test, count, original float coordinate calculation, and recurrence operation order; do not change compiler flags, approximate membership, or specialize to tested inputs. Overwrite the full output and validate smaller and shifted-bound cases. Use one-thread throughput as the main kernel comparison and report the four-core-budget result transparently rather than claiming thread scaling.
T3.subject: Scalar instruction-level parallelism via pixel interleaving

mission.hypothesis: With more than one usable worker, schedule(static) over rows assigns contiguous row blocks and may reduce dynamic queue overhead; however, Mandelbrot iteration costs can vary across those blocks, so static scheduling may also increase imbalance. The serial branch avoids OpenMP overhead for a one-thread team, and the requested team is capped by height. This contrasts with the prior dynamic-row experiment without changing the coordinate expressions or scalar recurrence.

retained: Extracted one row's unchanged float coordinate calculations and scalar Mandelbrot recurrence into a row helper shared by serial and parallel paths.
Added an OpenMP parallel-for over rows with schedule(static), using the default contiguous row partition.
Capped the requested team size by height and retained a serial path when the usable requested team has at most one thread.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: Dynamic scheduling of one complete row at a time may reduce imbalance from rows with different Mandelbrot iteration counts compared with contiguous static row allocation. The serial branch avoids OpenMP overhead when the usable team is one; capping the team by height avoids requesting workers that cannot receive rows. The recurrence and per-pixel coordinate expressions remain unchanged.

retained: Parallelize the outer row loop with OpenMP dynamic scheduling and chunk size one when the usable team has more than one thread.
Keep a serial nested-loop path for a one-thread usable team and cap the requested team size at the number of rows.

hypotheses.claim: Un ordonnancement guided pourrait réduire le coût de distribution par rapport au dynamic, chunk 1, tout en équilibrant les lignes de coût inégal; cela reste à mesurer.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Comparer guided (chunk minimal 1) au dynamic actuel, sans changer la récurrence, avec trois répétitions à n=1024 sur 1 et 4 cœurs, puis vérifier aussi des petites tailles et des bornes décalées.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Écarter guided s’il n’améliore pas de façon reproductible le temps à 4 cœurs, s’il pénalise sensiblement le cas à 1 cœur, ou si un contrôle échoue.

hypotheses.claim: Le schedule static contigu est une alternative utile comme témoin à faible coût de distribution, mais pourrait perdre sur les bornes irrégulières; aucune mesure ne permet encore de trancher.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Comparer static contigu au dynamic actuel avec la même récurrence et le même protocole, à n=1024 et sur petites tailles avec bornes décalées, à 1 et 4 cœurs.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Ne pas retenir static s’il n’apporte aucun avantage reproductible sur au moins un cas cible ou si la correction n’est pas préservée.

observations.claim: L’essai T1 est déclaré valide et correct, avec 0,2820825 s de temps moyen et un score de 0,66637; sa transformation utilise un schedule OpenMP dynamic, chunk 1, avec chemin sériel pour une équipe d’un thread et équipe plafonnée au nombre de lignes.

Le journal de correction rapporte 8 cas corrects (n=32 à 1024, patterns 0 et 1), sans erreur, avec entrées inchangées et gardes intactes. Les échantillons à n=1024 incluent 1 et 4 threads et sont également marqués corrects.
Le catalogue rapporte pour la baseline un résultat valide/correct à 0,5634215 s et score 0,5; les deux temps affichés sont des mesures de leurs essais respectifs, pas une confirmation indépendante.

uncertainties: Aucune comparaison de schedule static, guided, de granularité ou de tuilage n’est fournie.
Les journaux visibles ne permettent pas de confirmer explicitement que les cas de correction couvrent des bornes décalées.
Aucune confirmation indépendante n’est fournie pour le résultat T1.

Compute the supplied Mandelbrot iteration counts exactly for a width=(3*n/2), height=n image; input1 contains x0,y0,x1,y1. parameter is the maximum count (512); output is width*height int32 values. n=1024 performance; smaller checks and shifted bounds. No approximation of membership or iteration counts. Benchmark one and four CPU cores.

The harness measures native wall-clock time, excluding input generation, oracle and compilation. Search and confirmation use different seeds. Numerical tolerances are fixed.
